internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All three occurrences of b-r-H are first-person imperfect verbs, all negated (lan/la), and all followed by a hatta 'until' clause naming an end event. The root itself means 'to depart / leave off / stop doing'. Because it is always negated here, the whole phrase means 'I/we will not leave off ... until ...', i.e. a vow to stay put or keep going until a boundary. In 12:80 it takes a concrete place-object ('the land'), so it is a plain motion verb 'depart'; in 18:60 and 20:91 it works like a helper verb of continuance ('will not cease'), with 20:91 attaching a state ('being devoted', 'akifin') rather than a place. The persistence sense belongs to the negation, not to the root.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: brH does NOT itself mean 'remain / persist / stay' — that reading appears only under negation and is contributed by la/lan. It does NOT entail physical motion (20:91's 'akifin are stationary and brH governs a devotional state). It does NOT require a spatial object (18:60 is complement-less; 20:91's complement is a state). It is NOT the terminal/arrival event — the hatta verb (permit/reach/return) carries the terminus; brH marks the durative non-cessation before it. It is NOT the maintained state itself — in 20:91 'akafa (root 'kf) supplies the devotional staying while brH supplies its (non-)cessation, proving brH is a departure/cessation operator, not a stay-verb. Its affirmative sense is UNATTESTED: no positive token exists, so the positive nucleus is inferred as the polar complement of the attested negated form, not directly observed.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 20:91 نَّبْرَحَ governs the stative predicate عَٰكِفِينَ (a posture/devotional condition, not a place) while the devotees physically stay put, so برح here cannot mean locative departure and forces the abstract 'leave off/cease a maintained state' nucleus; conversely 12:80 أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ takes a concrete accusative place-object that a bare aspectual 'not-cease' auxiliary cannot host — the two poles mutually resist, and neither reduces to the other without importing the classical 'depart-place / cease-state' bridge, which is not demonstrated Quran-internally (no affirmative and no shared-construction control token exists).
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A two-lexeme splitting account: (a) a full motion verb baraHa 'depart a location' (12:80), and (b) a grammaticalized continuance-auxiliary (ma/la bariHa) 'still / not cease' behaving as a sister of kana (18:60, 20:91) — treated as distinct lexicalized functions sharing only a consonantal root. It is defensible on syntax (transitive full verb vs. copular auxiliary governing a predicate) and cannot be refuted Quran-internally because there is no affirmative or shared-construction token to prove one nucleus. It loses to the unified account only on parsimony and on the small, complement-mediated semantic distance ('quit a place' <-> 'not quit a posture', bridged by 20:91's postural complement), which is why unity is PREFERRED but capped at MODERATE rather than STRONG.

layer_attribution.derivation: All three carry qac_verb_form=null, i.e. base (Form I) finite imperfect verbs; the 'V' in form/qac_tag is the part-of-speech tag 'verb', NOT derivational Form V — no derived-form data is present, so no derivational-family claim is made.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: An affirmative (non-negated) or 3rd-person or nominal occurrence of b-r-H in which the root means 'remain / persist / stay' in its own right (not via a negator), OR a token in which negated برح plus hatta does NOT yield 'not depart / not cease until X' — either would show the persistence sense is lexical to the root and the departure/cessation nucleus is wrong.
rejection_condition.search_location: The full Quranic concordance for root b-r-H beyond this 3-token packet — specifically any affirmative, non-first-person, or nominal/participial derivative, and any occurrence outside the negated + hatta frame.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Read each additional occurrence's verse_text and qac morphology; test whether the root, stripped of its negator, profiles 'depart/leave off/cease' (predicted) or 'remain/persist' (would falsify), and whether the transitive-vs-continuance construction split recurs or collapses.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Isolate the root's contribution from the negator (la/lan) and from the hatta terminus clause and from co-occurring state verbs like 'akafa; attribute the persistence reading to negation, not to برح, before accepting or rejecting.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If affirmative برح profiles 'remain/persist', the departure/cessation nucleus is rejected and the root reclassified as an inherent continuance verb; if the construction split fails to recur, the lexicalized-class cap is revisited and scope may narrow to OCCURRENCE_LEVEL.

reopen_conditions: Any affirmative or non-first-person or nominal attestation of b-r-H is found (the corpus here is 100% negated first-person imperfect); test whether the positive root profiles 'depart/cease' or 'remain', since the entire nucleus is currently inferred as the polar complement of negated forms.
